verbatim:
What every line must pass.
Lead with what the reader is feeling. Then say what we do about it. Then say what they get.
Section 1
Four questions for every line.
Lead with what the reader is feeling. Then say what we do about it. Then say what they get. After the draft, run every sentence through these four questions:
01
Could a competitor paste this and have it be true? If yes, it is empty. Make it ours.
02
Can a real person picture exactly what happens, or is it a vibe-word?
03
Does this sentence say something the next sentence needs? And does it advance the story? If no, cut it.
04
Does it sound like us, or like any company?
Section 2
Two more checks the four questions don't replace.
Carry the because.
If the source gives the reason a claim is true, keep it. "We bring policymakers in alongside the builders because I have a background in politics" is credible. The same line without the reason is a bare assertion anyone could make.
Clearer than the source.
Hold your line against the quote it came from. If yours is vaguer or harder to picture, you went backwards. The raw quote almost always names something concrete ("get on the laptop and get on the playground"). Your job is to keep that, not abstract it away.
Section 3
Five writing techniques Rob uses. Copy them.
These are the specific techniques Rob Richardson uses. Copy them.
Wordplay and memorable names.
Frameworks get short, sticky names: Pain/Play/Practice, the three Fs, the three returns.
Metaphor and analogy.
"AI is a genius with no common sense or context, a nerd that can tell you equations but can't tie their shoes." (Rob Richardson, 2026-04-28)
Songs and pop-culture bridges.
An Oscar win becomes a lesson on being your unique self; test pieces on Michael Jackson and Star Wars. (Rob Richardson, 2026-03-20)
Show, don't tell.
"We can't tell people anymore what you can do with AI. Better to show them." (Rob Richardson, 2026-01-16)
Human story first.
Open on a real, often self-deprecating moment, then make the point.
Section 4
Six ways to open a piece (Rob's own opener catalog, 2026-03-20).
Pick one to open a piece.
01
Fortune teller. where this is going
02
Experimenter. I tried it, here is what happened
03
Teacher. here is how it works
04
Magician. the surprising result
05
Investigator. what is really going on
06
Contrarian. everyone says X; here is why that's wrong
